en: When you need structured outputs and you're
working with OpenAI and you're using Python
or JavaScript,
you can actually avoid the hassle of
defining this schema as I showed it to you
in the last lecture.
You can still do that as you saw, but you
don't have to.
Instead, when using Python,
you can use an extra library called Pydantic
to define a class that describes the schema
of the data you want the AI model to
generate.
So here I created an invoice class which
extends the BaseModel class, which is
provided by Pydantic.
And I define a bunch of fields in there,
which in the end just means I describe those
fields. The rest will be done behind the
scenes by the OpenAI SDK and Pydantic.
Now, the vendor and customer fields are
actually classes themselves since I'm
working with nested objects here, nested
dictionaries later.
And I brought back the OpenAI client here,
the OpenAI SDK. I no longer send requests
myself anymore.
Instead, in extract invoice details, I now
still have that prompt,
but the rest of the logic is way simpler. As
you can tell, it's way less code because
this entire schema definition disappeared.
Instead, I just set this special text format
parameter here
in the parse method, which I call on client
responses.
Previously, we used client responses create.
Now, if we wanna deal with structured data,
if we wanna get structured data, we use
client responses parse.
And that parse method supports a text format
parameter, which takes a Pydantic class as
an input.
So my
invoice class here,
that's sent to the OpenAI SDK, so to say.
And behind the scenes, that SDK will derive
that schema as we defined it in the last
lecture from that class here. And therefore
we don't have to do that on our own.
Instead, this will now generate a response.
We can then get the parsed response data in
this outputParsed property on the response
object,
and that will be an object of our class
which we defined here. So we'll get back an
invoice object here
in outputParsed,
and it's then this invoice object which I'm
using down here
to
insert it into the database. For that, I'm
using the model_dump method, which is
provided by Pydantic to turn this invoice
class into an ordinary dictionary.
And that's then inserted into my database.
And I still also print it to the console.
And with that,
if I now run this script again and I try to
read in all PDFs,
I still process them like before and they're
still sent to OpenAI
and I still get back the same result as
before. So the data is extracted correctly,
but now
I have a bit of an easier time writing that
code because a lot of work is done for me
behind the scenes. But again, that's not
necessarily available in all programming
languages and also not with all providers.
So knowing what happens behind the scenes is
always important, which is why I showed it
to you in the last lecture.

into the database, let's have a look. And
